version_history.subject: [PATCH] btrfs: keep unused block groups queued when a pass fails

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch addresses a potential issue in the btrfs file system where unused block groups can be leaked and lead to spurious ENOSPC errors. The problem occurs when an error is encountered while deleting unused block groups, causing them to be skipped and not re-queued for later processing. To fix this, the patch changes the logic of the deletion loop to break out of it when an error is encountered, rather than skipping the rest of the block groups. Additionally, it links the failing block group to a retry list at the individual failure sites, ensuring that it is not leaked.

review_comments.author: Qu Wenruo
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer Qu Wenruo questioned which error caused a non-zero @ret value in the loop and suggested that the issue might be due to incorrect reserved space checking by inc_block_group_ro() checks.

Reviewer noted that the patch's approach of breaking out of the loop when ret != 0 may not be sufficient, as it delays error handling to the next iteration.
review_comments.raw_body:
Do have happen to know which error caused this non-zero @ret?

I did a quick glance into the loop, it looks like it's not that easy to 
get a non-zero @ret:

- inc_block_group_ro() failure
   @ret is reset to 0, so not this path.

- btrfs_zone_finish()
   I guess meta is not deploying zoned btrfs in production.

- btrfs_star_trans_remove_block_group()
   This can return -ENOSPC, especially considering we have just marked
   one bg read-only, thus even stealing from global rsv, we may still
   fail with ENOSPC here.

   Although I'd say, that means the inc_block_group_ro() checks are not
   doing the correct reserved space checking, and that may be the real
   problem.

- btrfs_remove_chunk()
   If it failed, the trans is already aborted.

---

Otherwise the handling looks correct to me, doing the proper handling on 
error, other than delaying it to the next iteration.

Thanks,
Qu

version_history.subject: [PATCH] mm/madvise: reclaim isolated folios if PTE restart fails

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch addresses a concurrency issue in the Linux kernel's madvise functionality. When MADV_PAGEOUT is used to collect isolated folios, a concurrent operation can remove or replace the PTE table while the lock is dropped, causing pte_offset_map_lock() to return NULL and bypassing reclaim_pages(). The patch routes this failure through the existing cleanup path, ensuring that any collected folios are reclaimed or put back. This fix prevents a situation where isolated folios remain off the LRU with elevated references.

review_comments.author: Gregory Price (author)
review_comments.summary: The author is addressing a concern about the testability of mm/ components, specifically the page allocator and other parts of memory management. The author has been exploring various testing mechanisms, including selftests, Usermode Linux (UML), userland VMA tests, and the Linux Test Project. They have found that selftests are limited and create maintenance burdens, but have made progress in using UML and userland VMA tests to stub out reclaim calls and demonstrate basic correctness for a combination of commands into the page allocator. The author is optimistic about making test-driven development feasible with the help of Large Language Models (LLMs).

Yes, in fact I used that as a start for exploring how I might make other
components testable the same way.

"Stubs... stubs everywhere"

There's basically 4 testing mechanisms i explored:

1) selftest
2) Usermode Linux (UML)
3) Userland stuff like VMA
4) Linux Test Project (for syscall and ABI testing)

selftests are really limited and actually create a maintenance burden,
they're not real unit tests and are highly dependent on the actual
machine configuration which is super annoying.

But, lets take the page allocator as an example.

The only piece of the page allocator that "should" (cough, simplifying
here a bit) be machine specific is zone and node configurations... but
I'm not convinced that this should require a full VM to unit-test.

(other caveat: obviously some things like RCU and interrupt contexts are
hard in userland, putting that aside for now).

We should be able to stub out the reclaim calls and at least demonstrate
basic correctness for a combinatrix of commands into the page allocator.

Anyway...

I've been looking at how to use the VMA and UML test infrastructure to
stub out even more of mm/ and generate these kinds of basic contract
tests.  So far I've found bugs in a few random corners, but nothing
critical or reachable as far as i can tell - so that's nice.

Have made it compilable with ASAN and Coverage

The harness itself turns into a decent fuzzer as well for basic stupid
logic conditions, which in turn allows coverage and LLM guided fuzzing
into an easier task for any random kernel dev to start engaging in.

> atm. May set the LLM on it though...

On Sat, Sep 12, 2026 at 07:08:32AM -0400, Gregory Price wrote:
> MADV_PAGEOUT collects isolated folios on a local list before reclaiming
> them after the PTE walk.  The reschedule path drops the PTE lock and then
> restarts the mapping with pte_offset_map_lock().

Is this reschedule path even necessary? It's pretty bloody sketchy.

I thought the modern approach (TM) was to not do cond_resched() and friends so
can we actually look at removing this?

>
> A concurrent operation can remove or replace the PTE table while the lock
> is dropped, causing pte_offset_map_lock() to return NULL.  Returning directly
> in that case bypasses reclaim_pages(), leaving the collected folios off the
> LRU with elevated references.
>
> Route the failure through the existing cleanup path so any isolated folios
> are reclaimed or put back.
>
> Simplest userland pseudo-code reproducer:
>
> p = mmap(PMD_SIZE, ANONYMOUS);
> touch_every_page(p, PMD_SIZE);
> parallel {
>    while (1) madvise(p, PMD_SIZE, MADV_PAGEOUT);
>    while (1) {
>        madvise(p, PMD_SIZE, MADV_DONTNEED);
>        touch_every_page(p, PMD_SIZE);
>    }
> }
>
> Reproduced in qemu trivially with some explicit widening of the race window.
>
> Fixes: b2f557a21bc8 ("mm/madvise: add cond_resched() in madvise_cold_or_pageout_pte_range()")
> Reported-by: sashiko-bot <sashiko-bot@kernel.org>

> +++ b/mm/madvise.c

This function is truly some of the absolute worst code I've read in
mm. Shocking.

>  restart:
>  	start_pte = pte = pte_offset_map_lock(vma->vm_mm, pmd, addr, &ptl);
>  	if (!start_pte)
> -		return 0;
> +		goto out;
>  	flush_tlb_batched_pending(mm);
>  	lazy_mmu_mode_enable();
>  	for (; addr < end; pte += nr, addr += nr * PAGE_SIZE) {
> @@ -568,6 +568,7 @@ static int madvise_cold_or_pageout_pte_range(pmd_t *pmd,
>  			folio_deactivate(folio);
>  	}
>
> +out:

Seems odd to put this here for a condition that explicitly guarantees
!start_pte? It should be before the if (pageout) reclaim_pages(...);
surely?

I honestly wonder whether, rather than adding yet another label/goto into this
absolute bloody mess, whether we should just live with a bit of duplication and do:

	if (!start_pte) {
		if (pageout)
			reclaim_pages(&folio_list);
		return 0;
	}

I actually think that'd be clearer at this point than throwing in some more
indirection.

That's for the backport but somebody needs to rework this entire bloody
function going forwards...

Cheers, Lorenzo

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/4] mm: support promotion-only NUMA hinting scans
series_items.patch_summary: This patch introduces support for promotion-only NUMA hinting scans in the Linux kernel. It adds a new flag MM_CP_PROT_NUMA_PROMO_ONLY to distinguish between placement and promotion-only scans, allowing the scanner to choose whether to promote pages or not. The change is made to the mm module, specifically in the functions change_prot_numa(), task_numa_work(), and vma_set_file(). The patch preserves existing behavior for certain fixes related to NUMA balancing and memory tiering systems.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/4] mm: allow shared folios to be promoted to a fast tier
series_items.patch_summary: This patch allows shared copy-on-write folios and executable file folios mapped by multiple processes to be promoted from a slow memory tier to a fast one, while maintaining existing restrictions for ordinary placement. This change is intended to improve the performance of memory tiering systems by allowing hot folios on slow tiers to be moved to faster storage. The patch modifies two kernel files, mm/mempolicy.c and mm/migrate.c, to relax the checks that previously blocked such promotions. The changes are based on a previous patch (c574bbe91703) that optimized page placement for memory tiering systems.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 3/4] sched/numa: scan read-only file mappings in tiering mode
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access) hinting mechanism to scan read-only file mappings when memory tiering is enabled, but only for promotion purposes. This change allows hot file folios on slow memory to be tracked by the tiering code, improving performance in certain scenarios. The patch addresses an issue where shared libraries and other read-only file-backed mappings were excluded from NUMA hinting, leading to placement bouncing and poor performance. By scanning these mappings, the patch enables more accurate tracking of runtime load and improves overall system responsiveness.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 4/4] sched/numa: do not let VMA PID activity gate promotion
series_items.patch_summary: This patch prevents VMA PID activity from gating memory promotion in NUMA-aware scheduling. It introduces a new field to track the sequence ID of socket-placement scans and allows periodic placement scans to avoid starvation. The change is motivated by a scenario where a large shmem VMA occupied each scan, causing 84 GB of VMAs to be skipped as inactive. The patch fixes a previous commit that enhanced vma scanning logic and improves memory tiering in multi-threaded applications.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/3] mm/huge_memory: make thp_underused() work for mTHP folios
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the thp_underused() function to make it work with mTHP folios, which are larger than PMD-sized folios. The function is made size-aware instead of hardcoded to PMD-sized folios. A new helper function, thp_can_be_underused(), is introduced to check if a folio can be underused based on the number of zero-filled pages and the sysctl maximum value. This change will allow anonymous mTHP folios to be added to the deferred split list in future patches.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/3] mm/huge_memory: don't queue folios that can never be underused
series_items.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the handling of anonymous PMD-sized folios in the Linux kernel by skipping the queuing of folios that can never be underused, reducing unnecessary work and improving performance. The default khugepaged/max_ptes_none setting causes the shrinker to never split these folios for being underused, so they are not queued. This change is particularly important for a subsequent patch that adds anonymous mTHP folios to the deferred split list, as it prevents small mTHP orders from taking the list_lru lock on every anonymous fault.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 3/3] mm/memory: add anonymous mTHP folios to the deferred split list
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds anonymous mTHP (huge page) folios to the deferred split list in the Linux kernel's memory management code. This allows for underused splitting of huge pages, which can help reclaim unused parts of large memory allocations when the system is under memory pressure. The patch addresses a problem where fully mapped huge pages that are mostly zero-filled do not get split by the deferred split shrinker, leading to memory regressions. The solution involves mirroring the behavior for PMD-sized folios and adding a check to minimize overhead on common fault paths.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series addresses memory regressions caused by 2M THP=always on arm64 by splitting underused anonymous mTHP folios. The patches modify the deferred split shrinker to handle mTHP folios, which are not currently reclaimed when mostly zero-filled. Patch 1 makes thp_underused() folio-size aware, patch 2 keeps folios that can never be found underused off the queue, and patch 3 queues anonymous mTHP folios from map_anon_folio_pte_nopf(). The patches also adjust the behavior of khugepaged_max_ptes_none to make it an absolute count, rather than a per-folio order scaling factor.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v2] fuse: enable large folios
patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch enables large folios in the FUSE (Filesystem in Userspace) kernel module. Large folios are a way to allocate memory in larger chunks, which can improve performance by reducing the number of requests made to the underlying storage device. The patch caps the maximum order at the largest request that FUSE can issue, ensuring that each folio fits within a single request. This approach allows the allocator to fall back to smaller folios under memory pressure. Benchmarks show significant improvements in read and write performance for both tmpfs backing and xfs on NVMe backing.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v1 1/3] virtio_fs: zero the correct range on a short read reply
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the virtio_fs module where it incorrectly zeroed the unfilled tail of a short read reply when the read started at an offset within a folio. The fix is to calculate the correct range to be zeroed based on the descriptor's offset and length, rather than relying on an assumption that only holds for small folios. This patch also removes a WARN_ON statement that was added as a diagnostic aid but is no longer needed. The change is necessary to enable support for large folios in virtio-fs.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v1 2/3] fuse: drop rather than zero the copied range in copy_file_range()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the fuse:copy_file_range() function to use invalidate_inode_pages2_range() instead of truncate_inode_pages_range(). The change is necessary because once file systems support folios larger than a page, truncate_inode_pages_range() can zero out parts of the copied range, leading to data loss. invalidate_inode_pages2_range() drops the entire folio without modifying its contents, which is more suitable for this use case. This patch aims to prevent data corruption and ensure correct behavior in scenarios where file systems support larger-than-page folios.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v1 3/3] fuse: replace folio_test_highmem() with folio_test_partial_kmap()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch replaces the use of folio_test_highmem() with folio_test_partial_kmap() in the fuse module's copy functionality. The change is necessary to ensure accurate handling of high memory mappings, particularly when using large folios and CONFIG_DEBUG_KMAP_LOCAL_FORCE_MAP is enabled. Without this change, fuse_copy_do() could copy past the end of a mapping on a highmem build with the mentioned configuration.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series prepares the Linux kernel for enabling large folios in the FUSE (Filesystem in Userspace) driver by updating several places that assume a folio is a single page or that a page-aligned range is also folio-aligned. The patches are based on previous work and do not change behavior until large folios are enabled, at which point they will become reachable. The series includes three patches: one for virtio-fs, one for FUSE's copy_file_range function, and one to replace an outdated memory test in the FUSE driver.
